messages.subject: Using uninitialized variables
parts:
It was a stupid error of mine...
My model:

data {
  vector[N] x;
  ...
}
transformed data {
  real x_mean;
  vector[N] centered_x;
  centered_x <- x - centered_x; // !!!
  ...
}
etc.

The model compiled, sampling took a loooong time, results were meaningless.
Are such errors intended to be caught?

Thanks

Sergio

Ben

> The model compiled, sampling took a loooong time, results were meaningless.
> Are such errors intended to be caught?

I'm afraid there's nothing in place to catch the use
of uninitialized variables in vector operations. It
would slow them down considerably.

Some of the more complex functions trap and report on errors.
All of the distributions do. None of the C++ library functions
or built-in operators do.

We should develop a diagnostic in the parser that finds
the use of variables before they are defined.
I'll put that on the to-do list. It wouldn't be able to catch
everything, but the example you have could be caught.

- Bob

messages.author: 1cd3ce37d8489fec
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Using uninitialized variables
parts:
Hi,

I just wanted to chime in to say that I experienced a similar initialization problem.  I hope this note may be useful to others who encounter similar errors.

I had declared a convenience variable (real scalar) in my model section, which was supposed to be assigned a value via a series of conditional statements and then used to calculate the likelihood.  Because I mistakenly used only strict inequalities in the conditionals, the variable was never initialized in certain edge cases (i.e. where > ... and < ... both evaluated to false).  This resulted in stan segfaulting.

In retrospect, the error stan fails with (below) was actually fairly informative, in that it suggests a null pointer which was references by the non-initialized variable:

Signal: Segmentation fault (11)
Signal code: Address not mapped (1)
Failing at address: 0x8

But it took me a great deal of debugging trial and error (and, critically, the help of Dougal Sutherland :) to identify the culprit variable.  

My thanks to all of the Stan team for this fantastic package!

Best,

~Nathan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Using uninitialized variables
parts:
We shouldn't be segfaulting anywhere. Could you send us the
model that causes the problem?

We may have already fixed this --- I can't remember when
we added default inits, but it may have been after the 1.3
release.

- Bob

P.S. If anyone ever sees a segfault, let us know --- we want
to trap things in Stan before segfaulting. Segfaulting is
very poor behavior to calling programs like R or Python,
not to mention impossible for our users to debug.
